title: A pillow of arrows
hookLine: kings run up with soft pillows for the fallen grandsire, and he sends every one of them away
carry: the thousand names came from a bed of arrows
tomorrow: who leads the Kauravas now, and what does he promise?

cards: His body is held up by arrows, but his head isn't. It hangs down, unsupported. Bhishma asks for something to rest it on.
And the kings around him do the obvious thing. They run to their tents and come back with pillows, soft ones, fine ones, the best in the camp. Bhishma turns them all away.
These don't belong on a bed like this one, he says, in effect. Then he looks at Arjuna. Today, what a grandson brings instead of a pillow, and the last thing Bhishma asks of the war.

teach.b: Bhishma asks Arjuna for a pillow fit for a hero's bed, and Arjuna understands.

teach.h: LET THE WAR END WITH ME
teach.b: With tears in his eyes, the text says, he drives arrows into the ground beneath the old man's head, so it rests on them. The same grandson whose arrows brought him down.
Later, when he's thirsty, Arjuna shoots an arrow into the earth, and cool water springs up for him. Then he spends his strength on one more piece of counsel, to Duryodhana.
Let the war end with me, he says, in Ganguli's telling. Make peace with your cousins and let everyone go home. Duryodhana hears it and refuses.
The war goes on. But this bed isn't finished. Bhishma will lie on it past the end of the war, and when the fighting is over, Krishna brings Yudhishthira here to learn.
That teaching fills whole books of the epic.
One is called the Shanti Parva, the Book of Peace, the peace Duryodhana turned down today. And in the book after it, Yudhishthira asks: who is the one God, the highest refuge?
Bhishma answers with a hymn of a thousand names of Vishnu, the Vishnu Sahasranama. Hindus chant it in homes and temples to this day.
The teaching: in Hinduism an elder's last words are treasured, and the best of them lead back to God. Bhishma lost the argument for peace. He handed down a prayer that's still being said.

how: The Vishnu Sahasranama, which the epic places on Bhishma's lips, is chanted daily in many Hindu homes and temples, and paintings and carvings show Bhishma on the bed of arrows with his head resting on Arjuna's arrows.

o: the river Ganga carrying the fallen grandsire home to rest
the grandsire's end: a pillow of arrows and a last plea for peace
the funeral both armies hold together for their old elder

games.q: Bhishma on the field — tap the pairs.

s: Bhishma accepted the softest pillow in the camp
he sent the pillows away and let Arjuna's arrows hold his head.
Arjuna brought water up from the earth with an arrow
a stream of pure, cool water sprang up, and Bhishma drank.
he begged Duryodhana to make peace, and Duryodhana refused.

games.q: you're Bhishma on the bed of arrows, with Duryodhana beside you and a little strength left. what's your counsel?
o: make peace: let the war end with me.
win for me: avenge my fall.
say nothing; it isn't your war anymore.
games.why: Bhishma pleads for peace and is refused. after the war his teaching fills the Book of Peace, and gives Hindus the thousand names of Vishnu.

practice: The thousand names open with one word: vishvam, the whole universe. Many teachers read it as saying God is all of it. Sit back and let your breath settle.

Breathing in, think vishvam. Breathing out, let the word widen to everything around you: the room, the street, the people you love and the ones you don't. If you pray, let each breath be a name of God.
If you don't, let the word simply mean: all of it, held together.

wordCard.voice: Bhishma's fall. It ends with a pillow of arrows, water drawn from the ground, a plea for peace that went unheard, and a bed that will become a classroom.

orig.note: grandsire: the title the Pandavas and Kauravas use for Bhishma.

carryVoice: Your line: the thousand names came from a bed of arrows. Tomorrow a new commander rides out: Drona. See you then.
